provenance: Curated from the corresponding local Cambridge Task 1 chart or diagram image. These notes are canonical assessment evidence, not model-generated runtime OCR.

facts.title: Australian household energy use and resulting greenhouse gas emissions
factNotes: Energy use: heating 42%, water heating 30%, other appliances 15%, refrigeration 7%, lighting 4% and cooling 2%.
Emissions: water heating is highest at 32%, followed by other appliances 28%; heating produces 15%, refrigeration 14%, lighting 8% and cooling 3%.
Heating uses the most energy but is not the highest emissions source; water heating, appliances, refrigeration, lighting and cooling all have a larger emissions share than energy-use share.

facts.title: Sales of Fairtrade-labelled coffee and bananas
factNotes: Coffee sales rose most sharply in the UK, from 1.5 in 1999 to 20 in 2004; Switzerland rose from 3 to 6, Denmark from 1.8 to 2, Belgium from 1 to 1.7 and Sweden from 0.8 to 1.
Banana sales rose in the UK from 15 to 47, Switzerland from 1 to 5.5, Denmark from 0.6 to 4 and Belgium from 1.8 to 4; Sweden was the only decline, from 2 to 0.9.

facts.title: Destinations of UK graduates and postgraduates excluding full-time work
factNotes: For graduates, further study was highest (29,665), then part-time work (17,735), unemployment (16,235) and voluntary work (3,500).
For postgraduates, further study was highest (2,725), narrowly above part-time work (2,535); unemployment was 1,625 and voluntary work 345.
The same ranking broadly applies to both groups, but graduate numbers are much larger.

facts.title: Life cycle of the salmon
factNotes: Eggs are laid among reeds and small stones in the slow-moving upper river.
After about 5–6 months, fry (3–8 cm) move to the fast-flowing lower river and become smolt (12–15 cm) over roughly four years.
Adult salmon live in the open sea for about five years, grow to 70–76 cm and return upstream to lay eggs.

facts.title: Water use for industrial, agricultural and domestic purposes
factNotes: Agriculture dominates Africa (84%), Central Asia (88%) and South East Asia (81%), while industry dominates Europe (53%) and North America (48%).
South America also uses most water for agriculture (71%).
Domestic use is the smallest or near-smallest category in every region; South America has the largest domestic share at 19%.

facts.title: Places where people born in and outside Australia lived
factNotes: For Australian-born residents, city living rose from 50% in 1995 to 65% in 2010, while town and rural shares fell.
For overseas-born residents, city living increased from 60% to 80%; rural living became far less common and the town proportion stayed low.
In both years, people born outside Australia were more urbanised than those born in Australia.

facts.title: Average carbon dioxide emissions per person
factNotes: The UK is highest throughout, falling gradually from about 11 to 9 tonnes per person.
Sweden rises to around 10 tonnes in 1977 then drops markedly to about 5.5 by 2007.
Italy and Portugal increase; Italy reaches roughly 7.5 tonnes and Portugal rises from about 1 to just over 5, almost matching Sweden by 2007.

facts.title: Ashdown Museum visitors and visitor satisfaction
factNotes: Total visitors rose from 74,000 before refurbishment to 92,000 after it.
The combined satisfied/very satisfied share rose from 45% before to 75% after refurbishment.
Dissatisfied and very dissatisfied responses fell substantially after refurbishment.

facts.title: Australian men and women doing regular physical activity
factNotes: Women exceed men in every age group except 15–24, where men are 52.8% and women 47.7%.
Female activity is highest at 53.3% for ages 45–54; male activity is lowest at 39.5% for ages 35–44.
The gender gap is widest among 35–44-year-olds and narrows in the oldest group.

facts.title: Islip town centre now and planned development
factNotes: The current centre has a main road, shops, housing and parkland.
The plan adds a bus station, shopping centre, car park, new housing and a pedestrian-only central area.
A dual carriageway replaces part of the current road arrangement and the existing park is retained in a changed layout.

facts.title: Frequency of eating at fast food restaurants in the USA
factNotes: Eating once a week or once/twice a month are the two most common frequencies in every year.
Once a week peaks in 2006 at about 33%, while once or twice a month is highest in 2013 at about 33%.
Daily eating and never eating remain rare, at roughly 3–5%.

facts.title: Geothermal power plant
factNotes: Cold water is pumped 4.5 km underground through an injection well into a geothermal zone of hot rocks.
The heated water returns via a production well, enters a condenser and becomes steam.
Steam powers a turbine, which drives a generator to produce electricity.

facts.title: City Hospital road access before and after development
factNotes: The existing layout has a hospital on Ring Road, a staff car park and a public car park.
The proposal introduces roundabouts, a bus station, bus stops and a reorganised public car park.
Road access is redesigned to separate buses and cars more clearly, while the hospital remains in place.

facts.title: Households owning and renting accommodation in England and Wales
factNotes: Owner occupation rises from 22% in 1918 to a peak of 69% in 2001 before easing to 64% in 2011.
Renting moves in the opposite direction, from 78% to 31% by 2001 before recovering to 36% in 2011.
The two categories are equal at 50% in 1971.

facts.title: Electricity production and consumption in ten countries
factNotes: China and the United States are by far the largest producers and consumers; China produces 5,398 and consumes 5,322 billion kWh.
Most countries produce slightly more electricity than they consume, whereas Germany consumes more than it produces.
The remaining eight countries are far below China and the US, with Russia third in both measures.

facts.title: University Sports Centre present and future plans
factNotes: The sports hall and changing rooms remain in the future plan.
The outdoor courts are replaced by a leisure pool, while a dance studio and fitness room are added.
A sports shop and café are also introduced, increasing the range of indoor facilities.

facts.title: Sodium, saturated fat and added sugar in typical US meals
factNotes: Dinner contains the largest sodium (43%) and saturated-fat (37%) shares.
Snacks contain by far the most added sugar (42%).
Breakfast has the smallest or joint-smallest shares across the nutrients; lunch is generally intermediate.

facts.title: Export earnings and percentage change
factNotes: Petroleum products and engineered goods are the leading export earners in both years; engineered goods show the largest rise (8.5%).
Textiles record the strongest percentage growth (15.24%), despite lower absolute earnings.
Gems and jewellery is the only category whose export earnings fall, by 5.18%.

facts.title: Hydroelectric power station
factNotes: During the day, water flows from the high-level reservoir through reversible turbines to generate electricity for the national grid.
At night, the turbines reverse and pump water from the low-level reservoir back to the high-level reservoir.
The intake is open by day and closed at night.

facts.title: Grange Park in 1920 and today
factNotes: The rose garden, entrances and one water feature remain, but the pond, fountain and musicians' stage are removed.
Today the park has an amphitheatre for concerts, a café, a children's play area and an underground car park.
The layout becomes more recreation-oriented than in 1920.

facts.title: Coffee and tea buying and drinking habits in Australian cities
factNotes: Going to a café is the most popular activity in Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane and Hobart; instant coffee is highest in Adelaide.
Buying fresh coffee is lower than instant coffee in every city.
Melbourne and Hobart have the highest café figures (about 64% and 63%), while Brisbane and Adelaide are lower at about 55% and 49%.

facts.title: Tourists visiting a Caribbean island
factNotes: Total visitors rise from 1 million in 2010 to 3.5 million in 2017, with a brief plateau around 2015.
Visitors staying on cruise ships grow especially quickly after 2013 and exceed those staying on the island in 2016.
Visitors staying on the island rise to 1.5 million by 2013 and then remain around that level.

facts.title: Manufacturing instant noodles
factNotes: Flour is stored in silos, mixed with water and oil, rolled into dough sheets and cut into strips.
The strips are formed into noodle discs, cooked in oil and dried.
Finally, the dried noodles are put into cups with vegetables and spices, labelled and sealed.

facts.title: Destinations and salaries of Anthropology graduates
factNotes: Full-time work is the largest destination at 52%; unemployment is 12%, while smaller shares enter part-time work or postgraduate study.
Government-sector employees have the largest $100,000+ salary share after five years (50%), ahead of freelance consultants (40%) and private companies (30%).
Private companies have the largest $50,000–74,999 band (35%).

facts.title: Electrical appliances and housework hours
factNotes: Refrigerator ownership rises from 0% in 1920 to 100% by 1980 and remains there; vacuum cleaners reach 100% by 2000.
Washing-machine ownership rises overall but dips slightly around 1980.
Weekly housework falls steeply from 50 hours in 1920 to 10 hours in 2019 as appliance ownership increases.

facts.title: How sugar is produced from sugar cane
factNotes: Sugar cane grows for 12–18 months and is harvested either manually or mechanically.
The cane is crushed to produce juice, which is purified through a limestone filter and heated until it becomes syrup.
A centrifuge separates sugar crystals from syrup; the crystals are then dried and cooled.

facts.title: Southwest Airport now and after development
factNotes: The number of gates expands from 8 to 18 and the terminal gains a sky train, bag-drop area, cafés, shops and a new walkway system.
Check-in, departures, arrivals, passport control and customs remain but are rearranged or expanded.
The developed airport is substantially larger and offers more passenger facilities.

facts.title: How plastic bottles are recycled
factNotes: Used bottles are placed in recycling bins, collected by truck and sorted at a recycling centre.
Suitable bottles are compressed into blocks, crushed, washed and made into plastic pellets.
The pellets are heated to form raw material, which is used for new products such as bottles, clothing, bags and pencils.

facts.title: Norbiton industrial area now and planned future development
factNotes: The current site consists mainly of factories beside a river, road and farmland.
The future plan replaces factories with housing and adds roads, shops, a medical centre, school, playground and bridge.
Farmland is reduced and the area becomes a residential neighbourhood.

facts.title: Police budget and spending
factNotes: The total police budget rises from £304.7m in 2017 to £318.6m in 2018.
National government remains the largest funding source; local taxes rise, while other sources change little.
Salaries are the biggest spending item but fall from 75% to 69%; technology rises from 8% to 14% and buildings/transport stays at 17%.

facts.title: Average weekly family spending in 1968 and 2018
factNotes: Food is the largest item in 1968 (about 35%) but declines sharply by 2018 (about 17%).
Housing, transport and leisure take larger shares in 2018, with leisure becoming the largest at about 22%.
Clothing/footwear, fuel/power and personal goods all take smaller shares in 2018.

facts.title: Shop closures and openings
factNotes: Openings start high at about 8,500 in 2011, plunge to 4,000 in 2012, fluctuate and finish near 3,000 in 2018.
Closures peak around 7,200 in 2013, fall to 5,000 in 2015 and end slightly above 5,000.
Closures exceed openings in most years except 2011 and 2015.

facts.title: Percentage of the population living in cities
factNotes: Malaysia is highest from 2000 onwards and remains highest in 2040.
Indonesia starts lowest, rises sharply after 2000, overtakes Thailand in 2000 and the Philippines in 2010, and is second in 2040.
The Philippines peaks at 48% in 1990, falls to 43% in 2010, then recovers to 56% in 2040.
Thailand rises slowly to 33% in 2020 before reaching 50% in 2040.

facts.title: US households by annual income
factNotes: The $100,000-or-more group is largest in 2007 and 2015, at about 29 and 33 million respectively.
The under-$25,000 and $25,000–49,999 groups rise in 2011 then fall slightly by 2015.
The two middle-income groups change comparatively little across the period.

facts.title: Central Library 20 years ago and today
factNotes: The old library has adult fiction/non-fiction, children's books, a reading room, CDs/videos/games, tables/chairs and an enquiry desk.
Today it adds a computer room, café, lecture room, storytelling/events area, self-service machines and an information desk.
Adult fiction remains, while adult non-fiction is replaced by all reference books and the layout is modernised.

facts.title: Monthly change in prices of copper, nickel and zinc
factNotes: Nickel is the most volatile: it rises about 6% in January, then falls to around -3% in June before recovering slightly.
Copper fluctuates least, moving from roughly 2% in January to around -1% in mid-year and ending positive.
Zinc peaks near 3% in February, dips below zero mid-year and finishes with the strongest late-year increase.

facts.title: Participants in five activities
factNotes: Film club remains the most popular activity throughout, at roughly 60–66 participants.
Table tennis rises dramatically from about 16 to 55 and becomes second by 2020.
Amateur dramatics declines to about 5; martial arts changes little; musical performances grow from zero to around 18.

facts.title: Porth Harbour in 2000 and today
factNotes: The harbour changes from a mixed fishing/private-yacht area into a more tourist-oriented marina.
Fishing boats relocate, private yachts move into a marina and cafés/shops, showers/toilets and a lifeboat station are added.
The public beach, car parks, passenger ferries and castle remain, although their surroundings change.

facts.title: Biofuel production: how ethanol is made
factNotes: Plants and trees use sunlight and carbon dioxide to grow, then are harvested and processed into cellulose.
Cellulose is processed into sugars; microbes are added to produce ethanol.
Ethanol is used as fuel in transport, releasing carbon dioxide that is reused by plants, making the diagram a cycle.

facts.title: Dance classes by location and age group
factNotes: Private studios are the largest venue at 48%, followed by school halls at 24%, community halls/other at 18% and college-based studios at 10%.
Under-11s strongly prefer ballet (about 600 students), whereas 11–16-year-olds prefer modern dance (just over 500).
Tap attracts substantial and relatively similar numbers in both age groups.

facts.title: Population of Manhattan and other New York districts
factNotes: Manhattan rises from 60,515 (76%) in 1800 to 1,850,093 (54%) in 1900, then falls to 1,538,096 (19%) in 2000.
The other districts grow from 18,701 (24%) to 6,471,089 (81%) over the period.
New York's total population rises greatly, while its population distribution shifts decisively away from Manhattan.

facts.title: Beechwood Farm
factNotes: The farm plan shows existing agricultural buildings, fields, roads and access points alongside proposed visitor facilities.
The development adds accommodation and visitor-oriented areas while retaining core farm functions.
Changes should be described by location and replacement/addition, not as numerical trends.

facts.title: Little Chalfont Library members and loans
factNotes: Adults aged 18–64 form the largest membership group, while young adults are the smallest.
Adult fiction is the largest loan category (38%), followed by children's fiction (35%); all other categories are much smaller.
Total loans fluctuate around 15,000–20,000 before rising sharply to nearly 22,000 in 2016.

facts.title: How bamboo fabric is made
factNotes: Bamboo is planted in spring, harvested in autumn and cut into strips.
The strips are crushed to make liquid pulp, which is softened into fibres and separated into a finer fibre.
The final fibre is spun into yarn and woven into fabric.

facts.title: Jobs in four US economic sectors
factNotes: Manufacturing is initially the largest sector but declines markedly over the period.
Healthcare rises steadily and becomes the largest sector by 2020.
Agriculture declines to the smallest level, while retail rises to around 2000 then changes comparatively little.

facts.title: Chocolate production
factNotes: Cacao trees are grown in South America, Africa and Indonesia; ripe pods are harvested and the white cocoa beans removed.
Beans are fermented, dried in the sun, packed in sacks and transported by train or lorry to a factory.
At the factory beans are roasted, crushed to remove the outer shell, leaving inner nibs that are pressed to produce liquid chocolate.

facts.title: Formation of rain-shadow deserts
factNotes: Moist winds from the sea rise on the windward side of mountains, cool and form clouds and rain.
After crossing the mountains, dry air descends on the leeward side and continues inland.
This lack of moisture creates a rain-shadow desert on the leeward/inland side.

facts.title: Library user categories and satisfaction
factNotes: Full-time undergraduates form the largest library-user category, while distance learners and part-time postgraduates are much smaller.
Satisfaction is generally high for opening hours, staff helpfulness and availability of books/journals.
Reliability of the website has the weakest satisfaction result and the largest not-satisfied share.
